planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Catawbiense Album is among the hardiest and most reliable white-flowered rhododendrons for cold climates.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade, and mulch generously to keep the shallow root system cool and evenly moist. Rounded trusses of white flowers brushed with a faint chartreuse-gold blotch open in late spring against large, leathery, dark evergreen leaves on a dense, rounded, vigorous shrub. Selected from the native Appalachian species Rhododendron catawbiense, this old hybrid inherits exceptional cold hardiness and toughness, making it a foundational parent behind many modern hardy rhododendron hybrids and a dependable choice where winter cold limits other cultivars. Avoid heavy clay or poorly drained sites, water during dry spells, and prune immediately after flowering if shaping is needed.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; Cunningham's White is unusually tolerant of alkaline soil and urban pollution for a rhododendron.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; this old nineteenth-century hybrid is notably more forgiving of near-neutral or slightly alkaline soil and city conditions than most rhododendrons. Compact trusses of white flowers with a small greenish-brown flare open in mid-spring above rounded, dark green foliage on a dense, hardy, easy-to-grow shrub. Long valued as a tough, reliable landscape and understock plant, it tolerates pollution, wind, and heavier soils better than many finicky modern hybrids, making it a mainstay of older public and municipal plantings. Mulch to conserve moisture, water during dry spells, and prune immediately after flowering if shaping is needed.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Scintillation is a Dexter hybrid prized for refined flower quality and glossy, bronze-tinted new foliage.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade, siting it where afternoon sun is filtered in hotter regions. Full, rounded trusses of clear pink flowers with a subtle golden-bronze throat open in late spring above broad, glossy, deep green leaves on a well-branched, sturdy shrub. Bred by the amateur hybridizer Charles O. Dexter on Cape Cod and later introduced by Weston Nurseries, it remains one of the most admired and widely planted Dexter hybrids for its exceptional flower substance and dependable performance in the Northeast. Mulch to keep roots cool and moist, water during dry spells, and prune immediately after flowering if shaping is needed.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Anna Rose Whitney is a vigorous, large-growing hybrid popular on the West Coast.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade, allowing ample room for its eventual large size. Loose, open trusses of large, rich rose-pink, bell-shaped flowers open in late spring above bold, dark green leaves on a vigorous, upright shrub that can eventually reach small-tree proportions. Introduced in the 1950s and long a staple of Pacific Northwest and California gardens, it is valued for its strong constitution, rapid growth, and reliably heavy bloom in maritime climates with mild winters and cool summers. Mulch to keep roots cool and moist, water during dry spells, and prune immediately after flowering to control size if needed.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Jean Marie de Montague is a classic, widely grown red-flowered hybrid valued for reliable bloom.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade, and mulch to keep the shallow root zone cool and evenly moist. Dense, rounded trusses of bright, true-red, bell-shaped flowers open in mid-spring above broad, dark green, glossy leaves on a compact, well-shaped shrub. A French-raised hybrid introduced in the 1930s, it has remained a benchmark red rhododendron for nearly a century thanks to dependable heavy flowering, good foliage, and general garden toughness in maritime and mild-winter climates. Water during dry spells, avoid waterlogged soil, and prune immediately after flowering if shaping is needed.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Chionoides is a compact, cold-hardy white-flowered hybrid useful for smaller shaded borders.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade, mulching well to keep roots cool. Compact, tidy trusses of pure white flowers with a faint yellow-green blotch open in late spring above small, dark green leaves on a dense, low-mounding, slow-growing shrub. This nineteenth-century catawba-heritage hybrid has endured for well over a century as a dependable, compact white rhododendron for foundation plantings and smaller shaded gardens where larger hybrids would overwhelm the space. Water during dry spells, avoid heavy or poorly drained soil, and prune immediately after flowering if shaping is needed.
